chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Rawyani narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to us from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said:

Salman invited Abu Dharr (may God's mercy be upon them both) to his house and offered him two loaves. So Abu Dharr took the two loaves and turned them over. Salman said to him: O Abu Dharr! For what reason do you turn these two loaves over? He said: I feared that they were not well-baked. So Salman became intensely angry and said: How bold you are to turn these two loaves over! By God, the water that is beneath the Throne worked in this bread, and the angels worked in it until they tossed it to the wind, and the wind worked in it until it tossed it to the clouds, and the clouds worked in it until they rained it upon the earth, and the thunder and the angels worked in it until they placed it in its places, and the earth, wood, iron, animals, fire, firewood, salt, and more than I can count all worked in it. So how could you possibly fulfil this gratitude?
So Abu Dharr said: I repent to God, and I seek God's forgiveness for what I did, and I apologize to you for what you disliked.

key_terms.الشكر: Gratitude (shukr) — thankfulness to God for His blessings
key_terms.العرش: The Throne — the divine Throne of God, the highest point in creation
key_terms.رغيفين: Two loaves — two pieces of bread

ai.seo_question: What did Salman al-Farsi teach Abu Dharr about gratitude for bread?
ai.summary: In this narration transmitted through a chain of Imams from Imam al-Jawad back through al-Rida, al-Kadhim, and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them), Salman al-Farsi invited Abu Dharr to his house and offered him two loaves of bread. When Abu Dharr turned the loaves over to check if they were well-baked, Salman became intensely angry and rebuked him, explaining that countless divine agents and natural forces had participated in making that bread: the water beneath the Throne, the angels, the wind, the clouds, the rain, the thunder, the earth, wood, iron, animals, fire, firewood, salt, and more than could be enumerated. Salman asked how anyone could possibly fulfil gratitude for all this. Abu Dharr immediately repented, sought God's forgiveness, and apologized to Salman. This teaching illustrates the Islamic emphasis on deep gratitude (shukr) for even the simplest provisions.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: `Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Rawyani. He said: `Abd al-`Athim b. `Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to us from Imam Muhammad b. `Ali from his father al-Rida `Ali b. Musa from his father Musa b. Ja`far from his father al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (as). He said:

Salman invited Aba Dharr (rh) to his house and offered him two loaves. So, Abu Dharr took the two loaves and turned them over. So, Salman said to him: O Aba Dharr! For what reason did you turn the two loaves over? He said: I feared that they were not fresh. So, Salman became intensely angry and said: How bold must you be to turn these two loaves over! By Allah, I made this bread from the water that is beneath the Throne, and the angels worked in it until they tossed it to the wind, and the wind worked in it until it tossed it to the cloud, and the cloud worked in it until it rained it to the Earth, and the lightning and the angels worked in it until they placed it in its places, and I worked in it with the earth, wood, iron, animals, fire, firewood, and salt, and that which I cannot count. So, how could you show this type of gratitude?
So, Abu Dharr said: I repent to Allah, and I ask Allah’s forgiveness from what I did, and I regret my wrongdoing to you.
